title: Past-error scaling raised joint coverage of rebuilt NHC timed circles to about two-thirds in two basins in 2017-2025
abstract: We tested whether all timed NHC track error circles cover at once. We used official 1989-2025 error tables and radii fitted from earlier years only. In complete 2017-2025 forecasts at five times from 12 to 72 hours, joint coverage was 44.4% in the Atlantic and 44.9% in the eastern North Pacific. Each separate time had 69-73% coverage on the same cases. Scaling radii by the two-thirds quantile of earlier maximum normalized errors raised joint coverage to 66.2% and 65.9%. Quantile loss fell by 10.7% and 11.9%; storm-bootstrap intervals for the paired changes excluded zero. Mean radius factors were 1.31 and 1.27. Seven-time tests through 120 hours gave 64-65% scaled coverage. Equal storm weights gave lower coverage, so the sampling unit matters. This is a test of rebuilt timed circles on complete surviving cyclone cases, not the full plotted cone, all advisories, or impacts. Revised inputs and fixed fitted histories in intervals limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes, and an independent numerical check support reproduction.

display.caption: All tested timed circles cover in complete forecasts in 2017-2025. Bars show 95% storm-bootstrap intervals. The geographic cone union is not tested.

citations.reason: Public hazard verification motivates the question.
